mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increased by at least 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.0% indicates aggressive monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeded 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong economic expansion that boosts corporate profits and investor confidence, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO rose by at least 0.5% and UNRATE fell by at least 0.1% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (GDPC1 growth > 2.5% annualized and unemployment rate < 4.5%), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) relative to the prior quarter signals a weakening housing market that reduces consumer spending and corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth exceeded 2.5% and UNRATE was below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in real sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand that supports corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS increased by at least 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tight labor market that reduces corporate labor costs and increases profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE fell below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and a consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) growth rate above 2.0% annualized indicates robust economic activity and moderate inflation, supporting corporate earnings growth and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO rose by at least 0.5% and CPIAUCSL growth exceeded 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 3.5% and CPIAUCSL growth > 2.5% annualized), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) relative to the prior quarter indicates reduced consumer demand for housing, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeded 3.5% and CPIAUCSL growth was above 2.5%.
